applicability_resolution.note: All five trigger conditions were resolved from fields outside the gated sub-elements before any scoring, per the anti-circular rule. No condition failed, so no sub-element is N/A and excluded_max_points is 0.

conditions.evidence: description (E1): '2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)'; keywords (E1) include 'Diabetes mellitus'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes participant recruitment via 'an online REDCap recruitment interface' and e-consent.

regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (E2) = 'restricted'; regulatory_restrictions states NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security requirements and watermarking obligations that apply. This is an applying constraint, not a record that no restriction applies.
conditions.gates: Element 4 sub-elements 1-2 (already open via the human-subjects condition)

conditions.condition: Datasets shared and available for reuse
conditions.evidence: distribution_formats populated with format/media_type pairs (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown) and access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and .../access; license_and_use_terms grants a non-exclusive licence to download, reproduce, use and create derivative works for commercial or research purposes.

conditions.condition: Software tools produced as dataset output
conditions.evidence: external_resources (E10) references 'the GitHub organization of the AI-READI project at https://github.com/AI-READI'. This is an organisation root rather than a named repository, which is borderline; per the ambiguity rule the default is applicable: true and the sub-element is scored on what is documented.

conditions.condition: Data collection identified AND datasets shared
conditions.evidence: acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms both populated (12 mechanism_details entries naming instruments and settings), and the datasets-shared condition above is met.

issues_detected.description: No software is named for the transformations that produced the distributed data. preprocessing_strategies states in the passive voice that 'Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt files are converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT files are converted to the Open mHealth standard, and electrocardiogram data are stored in the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) format', but names no converter, pipeline or version. Every tool the record does name occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure are hosting, the RO-Crate/FAIRscape profile is metadata production, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data rather than its production. The GitHub pointer identifies only the publisher organisation.
issues_detected.recommendation: Name the conversion software and versions used for .fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth and WFDB encoding, and link the specific AI-READI repositories that implement them rather than the organisation root.

issues_detected.description: is_deidentified.method simultaneously reports that the FAIRhub dataset description records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' and that the public set is stripped of PHI 'using the Safe Harbor method', with identifiers_removed listing HIPAA PHI plus sex, race/ethnicity and medications. The two statements describe the same release and pull in opposite directions; the record flags the tension but leaves the structured method value carrying both readings.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the operative determination (HIPAA Safe Harbor applied, plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications) as the structured method, and relegate the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' registry label to notes with an explanation of why the registry flag differs.

issues_detected.description: variables is an explicitly partial inventory: eight substantive entries plus a 'Representative subset marker' entry stating that the complete variable documentation lives at https://docs.aireadi.org. No per-variable persistent identifiers (OMOP concept IDs, LOINC codes, column names) are given for any entry, so variable-level cross-dataset linking must be resolved outside the datasheet.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add OMOP concept IDs or LOINC codes to the listed variables and state the count of the full inventory, so the partial list is bounded and machine-linkable.

issues_detected.description: total_size_bytes (3,815,969,779,678) exceeds the sum of the nine datatype directory sizes (3,815,969,360,064) by 419,614 bytes. The record discloses the gap in source_caveats item (7) and states that the bundle does not explain it. The parallel file-count gap (356,343 total vs 356,334 across directories) is fully reconciled by the nine root-level metadata files, so only the byte discrepancy is unresolved.
issues_detected.recommendation: Recompute the directory byte totals against the release manifest and either correct the figure or state what the 419,614 bytes comprise.

issues_detected.description: Responsible-organisation conflict left unreconciled: data_governance.accountable_organization is Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and the licence names it as Licensor, while ethical_reviews and human_subject_research place IRB oversight, the reviewing body address and the reliance contact at the University of Washington. The RO-Crate label 'Washington University IRB' with a uw.edu contact compounds the ambiguity. The record discloses all of this in source_caveats items (2) and (3).
issues_detected.recommendation: Obtain a single authoritative statement of the sponsoring institution and the reviewing IRB, and record the other institution explicitly as a reliance site rather than leaving two tier-1 readings side by side.

issues_detected.description: The planned longitudinal follow-up fraction is given as both 10% of the cohort (NIH RePORTER and the FAIRhub study description) and approximately 4% (healthsheet). The record records both rather than selecting, and correctly omits the figure from collection_timeframes rather than asserting one.
issues_detected.recommendation: Resolve against the current protocol amendment and record the superseded figure with its date.

issues_detected.description: Two related_datasets entries use relationship_type 'is_described_by' with target_dataset pointing at journal-article DOIs (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) rather than datasets. The record itself flags that these targets are articles, so the slot is being used deliberately to carry an attested relationship the schema has no better home for.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move article references to a publication or citation slot if one becomes available, retaining the typed relationship for genuine dataset targets.

issues_detected.description: Two governance values are derived by the datasheet author rather than quoted from a source: confidentiality_level 'restricted' is inferred from the access model (the RO-Crate's own term is 'HL7:2N (normal)'), and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is inferred from statements that no identifiers were collected and Safe Harbor was applied, with no source making a compliance determination in those words. Both derivations are disclosed in regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats and are reasonable, but they are judgements rather than attested facts.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the derivation disclosure and, if possible, cite a source that makes the compliance determination explicitly.

issues_detected.description: No dedicated governance committee contact is recorded. data_governance carries committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact; the reachable addresses are the study central contact (contact@aireadi.org) under maintainers and the IRB reliance mailbox (hsdrely@uw.edu) under human_subject_research. A prospective user with a governance question has no named committee contact.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add data_governance.committee_contact naming the Data Access Committee contact for controlled-access enquiries.

issues_detected.description: No imputation_protocols slot is present. The substance is covered elsewhere: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states that missing values were filled only where directly derivable from other portions of an individual's record, under site PI approval, and otherwise left missing, with no instances excluded. This documents that statistical imputation was not used, but it is not discoverable from the imputation slot.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add an imputation_protocols entry recording explicitly that no statistical imputation was performed, cross-referencing the handling strategy.

semantic_insights: DOI 10.60775/fairhub.3 matches the 10.XXXXX/ pattern and the 10.60775 prefix is FAIRhub's own registrar prefix, consistent with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 — identifier, publisher and landing page corroborate each other.

NIH award OT2OD032644 parses correctly as activity code OT2 (Other Transaction, the Common Fund Bridge2AI mechanism), institute OD, serial 032644; the fuller form 1OT2OD032644-01 and the supplementary awards P30DK035816 and UL1TR003096 also match NIH patterns.

Funding purpose and dataset purpose align semantically: the award is titled 'Bridge2AI: Salutogenesis Data Generation Project' and purposes states the aim of insight into 'salutogenic pathways to return to health'.

Non-grant support is correctly represented without grant numbers: Microsoft AI for Good Lab cloud services and the Topcon/Optomed/iCare/Zeiss device loans and Heidelberg/Dexcom/Garmin discounts are recorded as in-kind contributions, so the absence of a grants block for them is appropriate rather than a gap.

Participant arithmetic is internally consistent at three levels: instances.counts 2,280 equals the split sizes 1,576 + 352 + 352, and the subpopulations distribution sums to 2,280 independently by race/ethnicity (380+545+519+836), by sex (951+1,329) and by diabetes status (776+560+686+258).

The subsets flags are semantically correct rather than merely present: all three subsets carry is_data_split: false because the enumerated subsets are access tiers (public, controlled access, mini-subset), while the recommended 70/15/15 split lives in participants.tsv and is documented under splits. A naive reader might expect true here; the false values are the right answer.

The absence of labeling_strategies and machine_annotation_tools is corroborated rather than an omission: description states the dataset 'ships without labels or targets' and 'no annotation or labeling was performed', and instances[0].label is explicitly false.

Temporal ordering is coherent throughout: collection 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 precedes the 2025-11-17 release of v3.0.0, and the three release dates (2024-05-03, 2024-11-08, 2025-11-17) are ordered with monotonically increasing participant counts (204, 1,067, 2,280) and sizes.

HIPAA Safe Harbor is an appropriate deidentification method for this data type, and the record goes beyond it by additionally withholding sex, race/ethnicity and medications from the public tier, with the re-identification risk assessment explicitly naming AI-driven inference as the residual threat and watermarking plus licence controls as the mitigation.

Human-subjects consistency holds in both directions: involves_human_subjects: true is matched by IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with a dated approval, a named reviewing body with address and reliance agreements, ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT06002048, written informed consent with a withdrawal mechanism, and a documented 200 USD compensation.

Consent scope and licence scope agree: license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is disease_specific_research and intended_uses restricts the public version to type 2 diabetes related research, matching consent_scope's statement that the public version may only be used for T2DM-related research.

Format declarations are consistent across three levels — root conforms_to_standard (CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE), per-collection conforms_to_standard on all ten file_collections, and the four media types in distribution_formats.

Bias documentation uses the BiasTypeEnum taxonomy correctly, with four distinct categories (selection, sampling, representation, measurement) each carrying a mechanism-level description and a specific mitigation, rather than a single undifferentiated fairness statement.

The record's systematic source_caveats discipline is itself a documentation strength: eleven numbered source disagreements are surfaced at the root with the ranking rule applied and the unreconciled cases left visibly open, and the pattern recurs at field level.

overall_score.denominator_note: normalized_percentage = 49/50 x 100 (adjusted base); fixed_percentage = 49/50 x 100 (fixed base). The two bases coincide because all five trigger conditions were satisfied and no sub-element was excluded.

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3; id: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.60775/fairhub.3; prior versions 10.60775/fairhub.1 and 10.60775/fairhub.2
sub_elements.quality_note: A registered DOI is present and carried consistently in three slots, with sibling DOIs for both prior versions.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Format check passes: matches 10.XXXXX/suffix. Prefix plausibility passes: 10.60775 is FAIRhub's registrar prefix and agrees with publisher https://fairhub.io/ and page https://fairhub.io/datasets/3. No RRID is present, which is not required by this disjunctive criterion.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project'; description (~2,000 characters) covering 2,280 adults, three named sites (UAB, UCSD, UW), collection window 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01, all modalities with their formats, 356,343 files totalling ~3.82 TB, CDS v0.1.1 organisation, and the public/controlled-access split
sub_elements.quality_note: Far beyond the 200-character threshold and specific throughout: cohort size, sites, dates, modality-to-format mapping, file counts and what is withheld are all stated rather than gestured at.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Description content is semantically appropriate for a multimodal clinical AI-readiness dataset and matches the keywords, instances and file_collections without contradiction. The stated 2,280 participants agrees with instances.counts.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: [Diabetes mellitus, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Electrocardiography, Continuous Glucose Monitoring, Retinal imaging, Eye exam, Data Sharing, Exploratory Data Collection]
sub_elements.quality_note: Nine keywords, above the five-keyword threshold, spanning condition (diabetes), methods (ML/AI), and specific modalities (ECG, CGM, retinal imaging).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Every keyword is corroborated by actual dataset content: ECG by the cardiac_ecg collection, CGM by wearable_blood_glucose, retinal imaging by four retinal collections. No aspirational or off-topic tags.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; file_collections lists ten datatype collections each with id, path, collection_type, file_count, total_bytes, description and conforms_to; subsets lists three access tiers with ids
sub_elements.quality_note: An accessible landing page plus a genuinely hierarchical resource structure: ten collections with per-collection counts and sizes, and a documented directory hierarchy of datatype/modality/device/participant.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Landing page URL is well-formed and its numeric path (datasets/3) is consistent with the DOI suffix fairhub.3. Collection ids use DOI fragment syntax (doi:10.60775/fairhub.3#cardiac_ecg) that correctly subordinates them to the parent.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four typed entries — is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2, is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.1, is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, is_described_by doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child id 4
sub_elements.quality_note: Version lineage is explicit and typed, with each target identified by DOI and described by release date and participant count. The parent/child relation to the mini-subset is also recorded.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Relationship types are used correctly for the version chain. The two is_described_by targets are journal articles rather than datasets, which the record itself flags; this is a slot-fit compromise recorded transparently, not a miscategorisation, and is logged as a low-severity issue.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'AI-READI Data License Agreement, Version 2.0, with Washington University in St. Louis as Licensor (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17555036)' with storage, secondary-sharing and derivative-work conditions; ip_restrictions.restrictions: 'Title to the data, and all industrial and intellectual property rights therein, remain solely and exclusively with the Licensor'; data_governance.access_review_process: 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'
sub_elements.quality_note: Access policy is operational rather than nominal: it states what a user must do (verified-ID login, T2DM-use attestation, licence agreement), where data may be stored (institutional servers or BAA-covered cloud), and what terminates the licence.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: The policy is internally coherent and proportionate to the sensitivity claimed elsewhere: a restricted confidentiality level and a controlled-access tier gated by data use agreement match the restrictiveness of the licence terms.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Compliance and Confidentiality Classification
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted; hipaa_compliant: compliant; regulatory_restrictions list citing the NIH Genomic Data Sharing Policy security best practices and watermarking obligations; other_compliance: not FDA-regulated (isFDARegulatedDrug 'No', isFDARegulatedDevice 'No'), no data monitoring committee, public release de-identified under HIPAA Safe Harbor; data_governance.accountable_organization ROR:01yc7t268
sub_elements.quality_note: Classification, HIPAA status and additional regulatory frameworks are all present and substantively described, with the RO-Crate's non-mappable 'HL7:2N (normal)' value preserved in notes rather than discarded.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Disjunctive criterion met on four of five listed paths. Gap: no data_governance.committee_contact or governance_committee_contact; the only reachable addresses are contact@aireadi.org (maintainers) and hsdrely@uw.edu (IRB reliance). Logged as a low-severity completeness issue. Both the confidentiality_level and hipaa_compliant values are author-derived rather than quoted, which the record discloses; the derivations are defensible and logged as a low-severity correctness note.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: [https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access] with notes 'Accessing it requires logging in through a verified ID system, agreeing to use the data only for type 2 diabetes related research, and agreeing to the license terms. Version 3.0.0 of the documentation adds guidance on Azure Storage access'; data_governance.access_review_process; page
sub_elements.quality_note: No root-level download_url slot is populated, but a dedicated access URL and complete, actionable platform access instructions are present, which is what the criterion asks for. A user can determine exactly how to obtain the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Evidence located outside the nominal download_url path, consistent with the instruction that listed paths locate evidence rather than require a particular representation. URLs are well-formed and the access path (/datasets/3/access) is consistent with the landing page. The record also notes that all files are readable with freely available software, so no hidden tooling barrier exists.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats entries pairing format with media_type: DICOM/application/dicom, CSV/text/csv, JSON/application/json, Markdown/text/markdown, plus two access-modality entries (FAIRhub platform download, mini-subset); file_collections give per-collection conforms_to and conforms_to_standard (WFDB, OMOP_CDM, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS)
sub_elements.quality_note: Both concrete formats and MIME types are given, and each is tied to the specific data it carries (DICOM for the four retinal collections, Open mHealth for wearables, WFDB for ECG, OMOP CSV for clinical).
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Media types are correctly formed and correctly paired with their formats. The format declarations agree across distribution_formats, file_collections and the root conforms_to prose with no contradiction.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four typed entries with DOIs; external_resources: documentation at https://docs.aireadi.org with a described contents inventory, project site https://aireadi.org with team/goals/contact pages, Zenodo community https://zenodo.org/communities/aireadi, GitHub organization https://github.com/AI-READI, CDS specification https://cds-specification.readthedocs.io/en/v0.1.1/
sub_elements.quality_note: Both halves of the criterion are populated and the external resources are described rather than merely listed, including the CC-BY licence on the documentation and a candid note that no persistence guarantee is stated for the docs site.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: All URLs are well-formed with plausible domains. The external_resources entry correctly observes that the dataset is self-contained so a documentation outage would not render the data unusable — a useful dependency assessment.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied: distribution_formats populated with access_urls to https://fairhub.io/datasets/3, and the licence explicitly permits reuse.
sub_elements.evidence: license: AI-READI custom license v2.0; license_and_use_terms: 'grants a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to download, reproduce and use the data and to create derivative works ... to enable reuse of the AI-READI dataset for commercial or research purposes'; data_use_permission: disease_specific_research
sub_elements.quality_note: Reuse is affirmatively permitted, including commercial use and derivative works, and the boundaries are spelled out: sharing only with identically bound licensees, BAA-covered storage, model release permitted where the model does not contain the data.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Not a standard CC licence, but a named, versioned, DOI-identified custom licence whose permissions and restrictions are stated concretely enough for a reuser to act on. Restrictiveness is consistent with the human-subjects scope and the disease-specific consent.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, WFDB, OMOP_CDM, ESDS, DICOM, OPEN_MHEALTH, RO_CRATE]; distribution_formats media types application/dicom, text/csv, application/json, text/markdown; file_collections each declare their format standard
sub_elements.quality_note: Every modality is delivered in a recognised domain standard rather than a bespoke layout, and the mapping from modality to standard is explicit per collection.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Standards are correctly matched to data types: DICOM for ophthalmic imaging, WFDB for ECG waveforms, OMOP CDM for observational clinical tables, Open mHealth for wearables, NASA ESDS ASCII guidelines for environmental sensors. Character encoding is not stated explicitly as a separate attribute, a minor gap absorbed by the ASCII/CSV/JSON format declarations.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: prose describing CDS v0.1.1 organisation and the per-datatype standards, plus 'An RO-Crate metadata file conforming to RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT and the FAIRscape profile 0.1'; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is stated at three levels — data organisation (CDS), per-datatype content models (OMOP, DICOM, WFDB, Open mHealth, ESDS), and metadata packaging (RO-Crate/FAIRscape) — with versions attached.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Schema URI is well-formed and resolves to the Bridge2AI data-sheets schema namespace, consistent with this record's own structure. Named standard versions (CDS v0.1.1, RO-Crate 1.2-DRAFT, FAIRscape 0.1) make the claim checkable.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: variables: eight entries (HbA1c, continuous blood glucose, best-corrected visual acuity logMAR, letter contrast sensitivity, MoCA total score, systolic blood pressure, step count, PM2.5) each with data_type, unit where applicable, measurement_technique naming the instrument and protocol, and quality_notes; plus a 'Representative subset marker' entry scoping the list and pointing to https://docs.aireadi.org
sub_elements.quality_note: The entries present are unusually informative — measurement_technique names the device and protocol (for example 'Dexcom G6 ... one measurement every 5 minutes over a 10-day at-home wear period; participants were masked to the results'), and quality_notes correctly distinguishes instrument reference ranges from observed minima and maxima rather than misfiling them.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Scored 1 on the strength of the descriptions and the OMOP CDM one-to-one table mapping, which is the operative mechanism for cross-dataset variable linking here. Two reservations are recorded as a medium-severity completeness issue rather than a zero: the inventory is explicitly partial (eight of a set spanning ~40 lab analytes plus questionnaire, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental variables), and no per-variable persistent identifiers (OMOP concept IDs, LOINC) are defined. The record is transparent about the scope limit rather than presenting the list as complete.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: two categories with examples and usage_notes, including the conditions for third-party model use under a BAA; prohibited_uses: six entries covering clinical treatment decisions, re-identification attempts, sharing with model vendors for training, onward transfer to non-licensees, bulk reproduction in publications beyond five illustrative figures, and watermark removal
sub_elements.quality_note: Guidance is specific and operational on both sides. The prohibitions are drafted as testable rules with reasons attached, and the intended_uses entry on model dissemination gives an actionable standard ('undertake all reasonable efforts to minimise the likelihood that data can be memorized, derived, reconstructed or reconstituted').
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Intended and prohibited uses are mutually consistent and consistent with consent_scope and data_use_permission. The distinction drawn between querying a BAA-covered third-party model and sharing data for model training is coherent and unusually precise. No discouraged_uses slot, which the disjunction does not require.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition satisfied on E1 and E8 evidence: description states '2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus'; collection_mechanisms (E8) describes recruitment and e-consent via REDCap. Governance condition independently satisfied on E2 evidence: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' with applying NIH GDS security obligations.
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.irb_approval: 'IRB protocol STUDY00016228. Initial IRB approval was received on December 20, 2022; the initial approval letter is published with the version 3.0.0 dataset documentation'; ethics_review_board: University of Washington Human Subjects Division IRB with full postal address and hsdrely@uw.edu, with reliance agreements at UAB and UCSD; ethical_reviews: three entries including named ELSI reviewers (Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman, Nicholas Evans) and Native Biodata Consortium engagement; regulatory_compliance notes ClinicalTrials.gov NCT06002048
sub_elements.quality_note: Oversight is documented at protocol-number granularity with a date, a named board with contact details, the multi-site reliance structure, and a separately documented ethics-review layer beyond the IRB.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Required consistency check passes: involves_human_subjects is true and IRB approval is populated. No data_protection_impacts slot, but the disjunction is amply satisfied and the DPIA-adjacent content (re-identification risk, mitigations, security classification) appears under participant_privacy. The RO-Crate 'Washington University IRB' versus University of Washington naming conflict is disclosed by the record and logged as a low-severity consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition satisfied on E1/E8 evidence; governance condition independently satisfied on E2 evidence (see sub-element 1).
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.method: 'No identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary ... The public set is stripped of Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule using the Safe Harbor method'; identifiers_removed: 'HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers (Protected Health Information); Sex; Race and ethnicity; Medications used'; deidentification_details describes internal review and the controlled-access holdback; identifiable_elements_present: false
sub_elements.quality_note: A named method (HIPAA Safe Harbor) is given, the removed identifiers are enumerated, and the record states which techniques were not applied (date shifting, non-arrangement of dates, k-anonymization), which is more informative than a bare method label.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Both required consistency checks pass: a deidentification claim is accompanied by a method and by an identifiers_removed list. Method appropriateness passes — Safe Harbor is the standard approach for this data type, and the additional removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications exceeds it. Content-accuracy tension logged as medium severity: the same field reports the FAIRhub registry type as 'NoDeIdentification' alongside the Safe Harbor claim. The record flags rather than conceals this, and the healthsheet's unanswered de-identification items are disclosed in source_caveats.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition satisfied on E1 and E8 evidence (description names 2,280 adult participants; collection_mechanisms describes participant recruitment). Participants exist, so the sub-element has a subject matter. The governance disjunct is deliberately not relied on here.
sub_elements.evidence: participant_privacy.anonymization_method (Safe Harbor plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity, medications); privacy_techniques: 'a robust data dissemination system, a strict licence agreement and static data watermarking that identifies the licensee ... these devices do not capture video or audio, are not equipped with GPS location monitoring and are not synced with participant-owned devices ... under a Level 3 data security classification'; reidentification_risk: 'theoretical risk of future re-identification, and notes that AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification'; data_linkage describes the controlled-access variables
sub_elements.quality_note: Protections are described at three layers — technical (device selection, encryption, Level 3 classification), legal (licence, watermarking) and organisational (restricted personnel access) — and the risk assessment names the actual threat model rather than asserting zero risk.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Required check passes: a re-identification risk assessment is present and paired with named mitigations. The privacy-by-design device rationale (no audio, video or GPS) is a substantive, dataset-specific control rather than boilerplate. The risk statement is consistent with future_use_impacts, which raises the same AI-inference concern.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition satisfied (see above).
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 and doi:10.60775/fairhub.1 with release dates and scale for each; is_described_by doi:10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x and doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449 with full bibliographic descriptions; subsets records the mini-subset as FAIRhub child id 4
sub_elements.quality_note: Relationships are typed, targets are DOI-identified, and each carries a description explaining what the target is and why it is related, including the note that v2.0.0 is no longer accessible.
sub_elements.semantic_validation: Version-lineage typing is correct and complete for the release chain. The two is_described_by targets are journal articles rather than datasets; the record flags this itself and explains that is_described_by is the relationship the sources attest. Logged as a low-severity semantic-understanding issue, not a scoring failure, since the relationship assertion is accurate even though the target class is not a dataset.

strengths: Exceptional ethics and privacy documentation: IRB protocol STUDY00016228 with approval date, named reviewing board with postal address and reliance contact, multi-site reliance agreements, ClinicalTrials.gov registration NCT06002048, written and electronic consent with a documented withdrawal mechanism and its candidly stated limit, 200 USD compensation with payment terms, and a re-identification risk assessment that names AI inference as the residual threat rather than claiming zero risk.

Replication-grade collection documentation: twelve collection mechanisms specifying device make and model, scan protocols, wavelengths, positioning, wear durations and sampling frequencies, with every named device matching the device folders recorded in file_collections.

Strong interoperability posture substantiated rather than asserted: seven community standards declared with versions, per-collection conformance, clinical CSVs mapped one-to-one to OMOP CDM tables, and a shipped Data Quality Dashboard artifact letting users verify OMOP conformance themselves.

Internally verifiable quantitative consistency: 2,280 participants reconciles independently against the three-way split (1,576 + 352 + 352) and against three separate demographic breakdowns, and the 356,343 versus 356,334 file-count gap is explicitly reconciled to nine named root metadata files.

Systematic and unusually honest source-conflict disclosure: eleven numbered source disagreements at the root plus field-level caveats, with the ranking rule stated, derived values flagged as derived (confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant), and genuinely unreconciled conflicts left visibly open rather than silently resolved.

Bias and limitations disclosure that is mechanism-level and typed: four BiasTypeEnum categories each with a specific mitigation, six typed limitations several carrying scope_impact or recommended_mitigation, and seven modality-specific anomalies explaining causal mechanisms.

Complete and coherent version provenance: three versioned DOIs with release dates and scale, the withdrawal of v2.0.0 disclosed, concrete inter-version changes described inline including a breaking change for reusers, a stated static-release update model, and nine raw data sources traced to their device export formats.
weaknesses: No software is named for the transformations that produced the distributed data. The .fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth and WFDB encoding conversions are described in the passive voice with no tool, version or repository, and the only named tools occupy capture, hosting, metadata-production or validation roles, so the release is not reproducible from this record.

The variables inventory is explicitly partial (eight entries against a set spanning roughly forty lab analytes plus questionnaire, imaging, waveform, wearable and environmental variables) and defines no per-variable persistent identifiers such as OMOP concept IDs or LOINC codes, pushing variable-level linkage out to external documentation.

is_deidentified.method carries two conflicting readings of the same release simultaneously — the FAIRhub registry type 'NoDeIdentification' alongside an explicit HIPAA Safe Harbor claim with an identifiers_removed list — leaving the structured value ambiguous to a machine reader even though the tension is disclosed.

No governance committee contact is recorded: data_governance has committee_name and accountable_organization but no committee_contact, so a user with a controlled-access or governance question has only a general project mailbox and the IRB reliance address.

The responsible-organisation conflict is unresolved: Washington University in St. Louis is recorded as accountable organisation and Licensor while IRB oversight, the reviewing board address and the PI affiliation in the RO-Crate all point to the University of Washington.
total_size_bytes exceeds the sum of the nine datatype directory sizes by 419,614 bytes with no explanation, in contrast to the parallel file-count gap which the record fully reconciles.
No imputation_protocols entry, so the fact that no statistical imputation was performed must be inferred from missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy rather than found where a reuser would look.
recommendations: Name the software and versions that performed each conversion producing the released data (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, ECG to WFDB) and attach used_software to the relevant preprocessing_strategies entries, linking the specific AI-READI repositories that implement them rather than the GitHub organisation root.

Add OMOP concept IDs or LOINC codes to the listed variables and state the size of the full inventory, so the representative subset is bounded and variable-level cross-dataset linkage is possible from the datasheet itself.

Resolve is_deidentified.method to a single operative determination (HIPAA Safe Harbor applied, plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications) and move the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' registry label to notes with an explanation of why the registry flag differs.
Populate data_governance.committee_contact with the Data Access Committee contact for controlled-access enquiries, keeping the general project mailbox for other correspondence.

Obtain an authoritative statement of the sponsoring institution and the reviewing IRB, record the other institution explicitly as a reliance or awardee site, and apply the same resolution to the disputed PI affiliation and the AI-READI name expansion.

Recompute the per-directory byte totals against the release manifest and either correct total_size_bytes or state what the 419,614-byte difference comprises, matching the reconciliation already achieved for the file counts.
Add an imputation_protocols entry stating explicitly that no statistical imputation was performed, cross-referencing missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy.
Resolve the longitudinal follow-up fraction against the current protocol amendment and record the superseded figure with its date, rather than carrying 10% and approximately 4% side by side.
